problem: The I_xx, I_yy and I_xy sums omit the parallel-axis terms of the wall areas. As written, a wall offset from the centroid contributes only its own centroidal second moment. The worked example correctly adds A y² for the horizontal walls and A x² for the vertical walls, so the formula and the example disagree.
fix: For a wall with area A_w = t s and centroid (x_c, y_c), use I_xx = Σ_booms A_i y_i² + Σ_walls [A_w y_c² + (t s³/12) sin²θ + (s t³/12) cos²θ], I_yy = Σ_booms A_i x_i² + Σ_walls [A_w x_c² + (t s³/12) cos²θ + (s t³/12) sin²θ], and I_xy = Σ_booms A_i x_i y_i + Σ_walls [A_w x_c y_c + (t s³/12) sinθ cosθ] (neglect the small t³ product term). These apply to the boom-plus-wall version; in the fully lumped version the wall area is already in the booms.

problem: The clause 'shear lag reduces stress in some booms, so the real load capacity is lower' is misleading. Shear lag lowers stress away from webs but raises it near webs; capacity falls because the peak stress is higher, not because some booms carry less.
fix: Say: 'Shear lag makes the stress uneven, with higher stress near webs, so the peak stress can exceed the simple beam-theory value; local buckling or crippling also lowers capacity.'
